title: Neverwhere
_plan: PHASE 1 SKELETON (2026-10-24): the branch spine from story-map-neverwhere.md, locked before any script, picture or voice. Each beat is a picture slot (still nw-<scene>-<word>, clip nw-<scene>-<word>-v) with a one-line caption and the people in frame (cast), not the final narration.

Numbering (owner, 2026-10-24): every scene id is <chapter>.<position in the chapter>: 9.4 is the fourth scene of Chapter 9, whatever it is (scene, cutaway, variant, dead end, ending; the title says which). Picture ids carry the same number. Choice ids are <scene>.<letter>. Each scene's `source` names its number in the story map. The full index is story-index-neverwhere.md, generated by app/scripts/scene-index.mjs.

Variables: LOYALTY is profile.traits.loyalty. DOOR_BOND, MARQUIS_TRUST, HUNTER_SUSPECT and ANA_ASKED are book vars starting at 0; the map's DOOR_BOND and MARQUIS_TRUST start at 1, so every threshold here is one lower than in the map (map 'DOOR_BOND >= 4' is vars DOOR_BOND >= 3).
Cutaways (titles 'Cutaway · ...') are the only scenes without Aurie; none runs back to back with another.
Cross-book echoes (ALEX_CURSED, Lucifer met, MATTHEW_RAVEN, Coraline courage) are text-only and added in Phase 3 when the engine can read another book's flags.

Dead ends (owner, 2026-10-24): scenes of type end with retryFrom; the player goes back with her state restored to how it was on arriving there. Each needs two wrong steps, or one the story warned about: 4.3 (gave Door away twice), 5.3 (grabbed the glass with no rat's respect), 6.4 (let go and walked on), 16.2 (crawled alone with courage under 3), 16.4 (took the kiss after doubting the marquis), 17.2 (gave Door up to the killers), 19.2 (threw the spear as in the dream). The Ordeal (14.2) and the angel walking free (20.7) go back the same way, to 13.1 and 15.3.
Owner's rule (2026-10-24): every ending and every dead end plays on video, never on a still alone.

Bridge from The Sandman (bridges.md, 2026-10-24): 0.1 opens differently for each Sandman ending, read with flagOn conditions: 'sandman:last=end-A|end-B|end-C|end-R' is true when end-A is the most recent of those four reached; 'sandman:@2.6' means a scene was reached; 'sandman:FLAG' reads a Sandman flag. Players who have not finished the Sandman get the first variant. Death (Aurie's sister) meets her at every dead end. Echoes: 2.2 Alex cursed, 4.1 Hob, 6.2 the Lyke Wake Dirge, 20.4 Lucifer, 21.2 Matthew's feather, 23.5 the shelf. The Sandman itself is not edited.

beats.text: The Dreaming is still mending around her, but the library stands, and on its far wall one of the three new doors has begun to rattle, as if someone were knocking from the other side.

At her wake they sang the oldest song for the dead: if ever thou gavest hosen or shoon, the fire shall never make thee shrink. The Dreaming kept her anyway, the way it keeps every dream it is not ready to lose.
Daniel, the new Dream, in white, finds her among the shelves. You always wanted to know, he says, what it is like to be one of them. One life. No idea how it ends.
Her realm is ash, and she has forever. The nightmares she can no longer hold drift out into the waking world, and one of them has found a sleeper in London.

She walked away from the Dreaming years ago, and has a life now: a flat over a bakery, an office off the Strand, a fiancée called Jessica, and a name nobody questions. Some nights she dreams of a library, and a door.

She keeps everything, and she will never change. So Lucienne brings her the only new thing in the Dreaming: a door that was not on the wall yesterday. A queen who will never change, Lucienne says, can still read.
Lucienne's report: a dream has come in from the waking world that belongs to no one here. A sewer. A boar the size of an ox. A spear, in a hand that is not quite a hand.
In the dream, a librarian she half remembers reads her a report: a sewer, a boar the size of an ox, a spear in a hand that is not quite a hand.
Someone in London dreams it every night and never reaches the end. A dream that nobody finishes becomes a door.
It is her nightmare. She will have to go in and fetch it back.
Among the carved doors, a plain London street door: peeling black paint, a brass letterbox, the Underground roundel worn into the wood.

To walk a dream from the inside, the Queen of Dreams has to become its dreamer: one woman, one life, an office off the Strand, and a name, Aurie Mayhew. She will not remember being anything else until the story ends.
She does not have to become anyone. She already is Aurie Mayhew. She has only to remember to open the door.
Lucienne: mind the stairs, my lady. They move. And if it goes wrong in there, you will only wake. Your sister will see to that.
The door opens on rain and pub noise.

beats.card: A small Scottish town · the night before London

beats.text: Aurie, sick at her own leaving party, sits on the kerb under a white umbrella printed with the Tube map. An old woman in shawls reads her palm: not any London I know. Beware of doors.

choices.text: Run after her with the umbrella.

aftermath.text: A good heart, she says, is sometimes enough. Mostly not.

beats.text: A girl has run four days through the tunnels. Behind her, two gentlemen in black suits walk their canary, Mr Ross.
Ross finds her. Her hand goes to his chest, and she opens him. She runs, bleeding.
Friday in the office off the Strand: trolls on the monitor, a Post-it on Jessica's photo. Late for dinner with her boss.
A dark street behind a high brick wall. A door opens where there was no door, and a figure falls through it.
Jessica steps over her. Aurie kneels; blood on her fingers. The girl's eyes open: not a hospital, they'll find me. Jessica: put her down, or the engagement is over.

aftermath.text: Jessica walks away in tears. At the flat the keys are inside; the girl touches the door and it swings open.

beats.text: Walking home alone at midnight, Aurie finds the girl still lying there, seen by no one. She carries her home after all.

2.1.title: Whose barony is this?
2.1.episodeTitle: Chapter 2 · Two gentlemen at the door

beats.text: The first Beast dream: a sewer, a boar the size of an ox, a spear in a hand that is furred and clawed, the charge, face down in bloody water.
Morning. The girl, in layers of filthy velvet and lace, stares at the buses: I'm in London Above. They bandage her arm at the sink.

canon: Door is hurt, grateful and guarded; she will not go to a hospital or the police.
Most of the blood was someone else's.
Nothing here reveals who she is beyond her first name, which she gives only after the two gentlemen have been.
conversation.opening: I'm in London Above. That's... not where I meant to be.

exits.2.1.A: Aurie helps without asking who she is.
exits.2.1.B: Aurie insists on a doctor and the police.
exits.2.1.C: Aurie makes a joke of the whole thing.

choices.text: You need a doctor. And the police.

beats.text: Mr Croup, small and orange-haired, and Mr Vandemar, huge, in black suits cut two centuries wrong, with posters: HAVE YOU SEEN THIS GIRL? Croup's smile arrives a fraction late.
Vandemar sniffs, walks straight to the bathroom. It is spotlessly empty.
Vandemar, sniffing the air: we heard of a man who dreams of waking. Nasty.

canon: They want the girl, alive. They are polite until they are not.
Croup cuts the phone line whatever Aurie says.
The girl is hiding and can hear everything.
conversation.opening: CROUP: Good morning, madam. We are looking for our sister. Doreen. A troubled child.

exits.2.2.A: Aurie says she has not seen her.
exits.2.2.B: Aurie threatens them with the police.
exits.2.2.C: Aurie glances at the bathroom and gives the girl away.

aftermath.text: Jessica's message on the machine ends the engagement. The girl is making tea. I'm Door.
Croup cuts the phone line anyway. Later: Jessica's message, and a girl making tea. I'm Door.

choices.text: She was here. In the bathroom.
choices.remembered: Door heard that. So did Mr Croup.

aftermath.text: They find nothing, and leave. The girl comes out of the wall behind the bath and does not look at Aurie for a long time. I'm Door.

beats.text: Door ties a note to a pigeon with Aurie's blue rubber band: find the marquis de Carabas.
A rat runs from the videotapes. Aurie throws the remote at it. It was carrying the reply.

choices.text: Apologise to the rat. With dignity.

beats.text: An alley that should not exist under one gas jet. Aurie turns three times widdershins and tosses the note at a bin; a pile of rags stands up and catches it.
The marquis de Carabas, in a coat with more pockets than a coat could hold.

canon: The marquis trades in favours and never answers a question directly.
He will help Door for a favour; what Aurie offers shapes how much he trusts her.
conversation.opening: And what, exactly, is the lady Door offering me?

exits.3.1.A: A favour. A really big one.
exits.3.1.B: She'll owe you. So will I.
exits.3.1.C: Aurie bluffs that Door can pay.

choices.text: A favour. A really big one.
She'll owe you. So will I.
She can pay. Whatever you want.

beats.text: A sewer ladder that comes out on a rooftop in daylight. London tiny below. The marquis lets go with both hands and waggles his fingers.

aftermath.text: On the roof Old Bailey offers starling stew; the marquis forces a silver box on him. A broom cupboard lets them out in Aurie's own stairwell.
He gives none, but he waits. On the roof Old Bailey offers starling stew; the marquis forces a silver box on him.

beats.text: Door, washed, in a huge leather flying jacket. The marquis kneels: my lady. She kisses Aurie's cheek as friends do and says sorry without saying for what. When Aurie looks up, nobody is there.
A taxi, a ticket machine, the Tube doors, Sylvia, Gary: nobody sees her. In the shop glass her reflection lags half a beat behind.
Only one person in London looks straight at her: a man outside the White Horse, who has drunk in that pub since 1389. He raises his glass. I know you, he says, puzzled. From somewhere.
Jessica's office, Angels over England posters. She apologises for her dreadful memory for faces.

choices.text: I'm sorry I upset you. I'd stop for her again.

aftermath.text: She calls after her: Aurie... Maybury?

beats.text: An agent shows the flat to a couple while Aurie hides behind a washcloth in the bath. We'll take it.
The phone. Through static, Mr Croup asks whether she knows what her own liver tastes like.

canon: Croup cannot reach her yet; he wants to know where Door is.
The operator cannot hear Aurie if she dials the police.
conversation.opening: Do you know what your own liver tastes like, Mistress Mayhew? Because it's one of the things we could find out together.

exits.4.2.A: Aurie says she does not know where Door is.
exits.4.2.B: Aurie offers to help them find Door.
exits.4.2.C: Aurie says she is calling the police.

choices.text: I don't know where she is.
If I help you find her, will you leave me alone?

beats.text: Croup, delighted: twice helpful, Mistress Mayhew. Vandemar: we don't need the other one. The line goes dead; the flat door opens on its own.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You don't die in a dream, little sister, Death says. You wake. Go back, and choose better.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You did this properly once, Death says. This isn't that. Go back.
Giving her away once was weakness. Twice was a contract, and they collect. The story goes back to the two gentlemen at the door.
The card is rejected. Aurie gives it to a short old homeless man: fifteen hundred in there, if you can get to it. He hands it back. He can see her.

aftermath.text: Iliaster hisses her back and leads her down basement steps.

choices.text: Grab his sleeve. Where is the Floating Market?

beats.text: He flees. Aurie sleeps on a bench.
Near dawn a rat leads her to the same basement door.
Near dawn Iliaster comes back, grumbling, and leads her to the basement door after all.
A sub-cellar. Croup throws razor blades between his fingers; Vandemar pins his own hand to the wall with his knife. The Bakelite phone: the employer wants the Door female, alive.
Vandemar spits on the wound, and it closes.
A vaulted hall of small fires and spits. A glass dagger at her throat. Across the hall people fall to the floor as a small black shape approaches: a rat, who seems to wink.

canon: The Rat-speaker serves Master Longtail and will do what the rat decides.
Aurie's bag is taken whatever she does; a girl is ordered to guide her to the market.
conversation.opening: Upworlder. You are in the hall of the Rat-speakers, and you will explain yourself to Master Longtail, or you will not.

exits.5.2.A: Aurie greets the rat and asks it about Door.
exits.5.2.B: Aurie kneels with everyone and waits.
exits.5.2.C: Aurie grabs for the glass dagger.

choices.text: Hello, Ratty. Do you know where Door is?

aftermath.text: Horror in the room, amusement in the rat. The bag goes; a thin girl is told to guide her to the market.
Without the rat's respect the Rat-speaker gets his nick in.
The bag goes; a thin girl is told to guide her to the market.
A cut on the neck before Longtail stops it. The bag goes; a thin girl is told to guide her to the market.

beats.text: Her hand closes on the glass; the Rat-speaker's closes first. Master Longtail does not stop him, because no one in this hall has ever seen her be polite to a rat.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You don't die in a dream, little sister, Death says. You wake. Go back, and choose better.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You did this properly once, Death says. This isn't that. Go back.
The story goes back to the cash machine.
A white hall hung with pictures of rooms. Memories in the walls: her brother in a Victorian pool; her mother and sister watering plants until Croup steps in.
Her father's study. The marquis pockets a small obsidian beast from the desk.
The journal machine: Lord Portico, bleeding. Go to Islington. Trust Islington. Avenge us.
Elsewhere, Croup and Vandemar hire Varney by pulling his morning-star apart link by link.
The girl wears a stained badge, I AM 11, and quartz beads. Do you like cat? Thigh or breast?
A bench on the Embankment; the Albert Bridge in its lights. Nobody ever gets both.

canon: Anaesthesia tells her own history in her own words, over a still two-shot; nothing is shown.
She is taking Aurie to the Floating Market by way of Night's Bridge.
conversation.opening: You don't eat much, do you? I ate your fruit. Was that wrong?

exits.6.1.A: Aurie asks about her, and listens.
exits.6.1.B: Aurie talks about her own job and fiancée.
exits.6.1.C: Aurie promises to get her back up here one day.

choices.text: Tell me about you. I'm listening.
Talk about your job and your fiancée.
I'll get you back up here one day. I promise.

beats.text: Varney's gang shoves Aurie down; Anaesthesia hisses like a cornered rat and Varney backs off. A tall woman in mottled leather joins them.
A stone bridge over a void. The dark is turned up. Something slithers past; Anaesthesia's hand shakes in hers. An angel falls with burning wings. The candle flares.
From somewhere, a song she cannot place: from Brig o' Dread when thou may'st pass, every night and all.
They sang it at her wake. She does not know how she knows that.

choices.text: Hold her hand tighter and keep walking.
Let go to shield your face.
Call her name into the dark.

beats.text: Nobody is holding her hand. Beads patter down the bridge. The woman in leather: the bridge takes its toll.

choices.text: Go back onto the bridge for her.

aftermath.text: The woman hauls her back by the collar; the beads roll into the dark.

beats.text: She let go in the dark and would not look back for the beads. The bridge takes its toll, and tonight it takes two. The woman in leather walks on alone.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You don't die in a dream, little sister, Death says. You wake. Go back, and choose better.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You did this properly once, Death says. This isn't that. Go back.
The story goes back to the Embankment, and Anaesthesia.
Knightsbridge; her watch has gone blank and she bins it. Harrods' Egyptian Room ablaze: dream sellers, a knight selling lost property, a dentist with a hand drill.
A pale woman in black velvet smiles at her.
A sign: OLD BAILEY'S BIRDS AND INFORMATION. The bodyguard auditions, he says, are in the Food Halls. What'll you give me?

aftermath.text: He waves it like a flag.

beats.text: The Fish and Meat Hall, sawdust. Bodyguards fight by knack; a thrown Ruislip lands on Aurie.
Late, Aurie sees only the end of it.
The leather woman puts Varney down with his own knife. I'm called Hunter. The Hunter? I'm back.
Door, on the smoked-salmon counter, furious: what is she doing here?

canon: Door is angry because Aurie is in danger because of her.
Hunter has just been hired as bodyguard; the marquis is here.
conversation.opening: Why did you have to come here? Why couldn't you just stay where you were safe?

exits.7.3.A: Aurie says she did not have much choice.
exits.7.3.B: Aurie says she came to find her.
exits.7.3.C: Aurie says Door knew this would happen to her.

choices.text: I didn't really have much choice.
You knew this would happen to me.

beats.text: The marquis explains the two Londons: Aurie has fallen through the cracks. Good night. She follows down the ladder. Go away. No. They leave her.

aftermath.text: She cries, for the first time since her father died.

beats.text: She keeps their lamp in sight through two tunnels, then loses it at a fork and sits down in the dark.
Varney flees down a spiral stair; Vandemar waits at the bottom paring his nails with Varney's machete; Croup falls on him.
In a tunnel Door stops: we can't leave her. The marquis: of course we can; we did. You are working for me, aren't you?
A ledge above a storm drain. Her lamp finds Aurie. She says sorry, and means it.

canon: Door came back for her against the marquis's advice.
They are looking for an angel named Islington.
Door can promise to try to get Aurie home, not more.
conversation.opening: I'm sorry. I shouldn't have left you. Are you coming?

exits.8.4.A: Aurie says she has nowhere else to be.
exits.8.4.B: Aurie will come only if Door gets her home.
exits.8.4.C: Aurie says no, and Door sits beside her in silence until she asks again.

choices.text: I don't have anywhere else to be. Why not?

aftermath.text: She hugs her and promises to try to get her home. They are looking for an angel. Aurie laughs until it echoes.

choices.text: Only if you get me home.

aftermath.text: She promises, carefully. They are looking for an angel. Aurie laughs until it echoes.
Door sits beside her in silence. After a while she asks again, and this time Aurie gets up.

beats.text: A rock hall, iron pillars, a waterfall, a black door of flint and silver. Candles light as a small barefoot woman in white passes, and go out behind her. No wings. Unmistakably an angel.
Hunter: there are shepherds in Shepherd's Bush; pray you never meet them. In the Bank tunnel the busker Lear can see them. The marquis plays a reel that empties passers-by's pockets onto his coat.
He taps Angel on the Tube map. Islington.

choices.text: There are no such things as angels.

beats.text: A Central Line platform. Hunter: mind the gap. Black smoke wells over the edge.

choices.text: Step back when Hunter warns you.

aftermath.text: The smoke snaps at nothing. Door holds her hand while she shakes.
It wraps her ankle; Hunter beats it off. Her jeans bleach where it touched; purple welts. Door holds her hand while she shakes.

beats.text: The hospital courtyard of junk and frogs. The employer's orders: scare her, not kill her. Crows overhead: a murder.
A dark, empty-looking carriage that inside is a medieval court: straw, chickens, a log fire, a wolfhound, old men-at-arms in knitted chain mail. The one-eyed earl in dressing gown and slippers.
The earl recognises the marquis, and his eye, and orders him seized.

canon: The earl holds an old grudge against the marquis (the White City retreat, his eye).
Door can invoke her house; the marquis leaves at the next station either way.
conversation.opening: Mooncalf! Who brought the marquis de Carabas into my court? Speak, or Tooley shall be funny at you.

exits.9.4.B: Aurie speaks up for the marquis.
exits.9.4.C: Aurie agrees the marquis seems dodgy.

choices.text: Say nothing. Let Door handle it.
He's with us. Leave him be.
He does seem a bit dodgy.

beats.text: Behind the throne, a stone library of lost property: dentures, gnomes, umbrellas, a wooden leg; Tube tunnels rushing past the windows.

aftermath.text: She gets the scroll: use the Angelus. They are dropped at BRITISH MUSEUM. There isn't one, says Aurie. Then be very careful getting off, says the delighted earl.
The scroll: use the Angelus. They are dropped at BRITISH MUSEUM. Be very careful getting off, says the delighted earl.

9.6.title: Cutaway · The Great Beast of London

beats.text: Lear mobbed by blank-eyed people forcing money on him; the marquis plays the counter-charm and calls in a theft.

Old Bailey's roof facing St Paul's. He names the obsidian figure: the Great Beast of London, a butcher's animal that escaped into the Fleet Ditch and grew. The marquis drops off the roof: keep the box.
A sealed station, 1930s posters for malted drinks. A rat, Miss Whiskers. Door opens an iron door: we're openers.

aftermath.text: Taken as tribute, the rat says. Sometimes they come back.

beats.text: Hunter will not go Above. She guards Door Below and cannot climb; a curse, she admits, like an embarrassing illness.

choices.text: Then wait. We'll come back for you.
What happens to you up there?

beats.text: Croup and Vandemar on plinths among museum junk. To Door: a traitor in your nest, a cuckoo.
Croup thanks Mistress Mayhew for her help, in front of Door.

canon: They are here to frighten Door, not to kill her.
If TOLD_CV is set, Croup has just thanked Aurie for her earlier help, in front of Door.
conversation.opening: CROUP: There's a traitor in your nest, my lady. A cuckoo. VANDEMAR: Cuckoo.

exits.10.3.A: Aurie puts herself between them and Door.
exits.10.3.B: Aurie grabs Door's hand and runs.

choices.text: If you want to hurt her, you'll have to kill me first.

aftermath.text: Vandemar, pleased: all right. Thanks. They run; behind them, cuckoo calls and a wolf's howl.
Behind them, cuckoo calls and a wolf's howl.

beats.text: Outside, catching their breath. A traitor?
The exhibition launch: a string quartet, champagne, a room crowded with angels, Jessica in green silk running the night. She half-recognises Aurie.

canon: Jessica cannot remember Aurie but feels she should.
Reminding her, gently or cheekily, ends with her sending for security; saying nothing does not.
conversation.opening: I'm so sorry, I'm dreadful with faces. Are you with the caterers?

exits.10.5.A: Aurie tells her who she was, gently.
exits.10.5.B: Aurie tells her cheekily: her birthday, the song she hums.
exits.10.5.C: Aurie says nothing and walks away.

choices.text: We were engaged, Jess. Until three weeks ago.
Your birthday's the twelfth. You hum when you're nervous. You're humming now.

beats.text: Mr Stockton pulls the cord: a cathedral door carved with a staring medieval angel.
Guards grip Aurie. Door screams into the microphone like a power drill.
Nobody stops them. Door's hand on the door; light like fireworks.

aftermath.text: Wrong London. Her hand on the door; light like fireworks; they walk into it, and the room agrees it never happened.
She screams anyway, and will not go without her. Light like fireworks; they walk into it.

choices.text: Walk into the light with her.

beats.text: The rock hall. Islington, small and golden-haired and sweet-faced as a girl, with eyes of old grey light, pours wine from Atlantis like a sacrament. To former glories.
She gives Door a black Beast statuette to bring her safely back, and asks for the key the Black Friars keep.

canon: Islington is gentle, patient and gives no hint of what she wants beyond the key.
It asks Aurie what she wants; the answer is remembered.
conversation.opening: And you, Aurie Mayhew? What is it that you want?

exits.11.1.A: Aurie asks for her life back.
exits.11.1.B: Aurie asks only that Door be helped.
exits.11.1.C: Aurie asks why an angel lives under London.

choices.text: My life back. My flat. My job.

aftermath.text: That can happen.

choices.text: Why does an angel live under London?

aftermath.text: She tells of the waves, and of a first city that sank.

beats.text: Drunk on Atlantean wine, on the museum steps at dawn. Door giggles.

aftermath.text: Door joins in, dances better, and they tumble at the bottom laughing. Hunter, at the station: they are very drunk.
Dignity lasts eleven steps. Hunter, at the station: they are very drunk.

beats.text: The marquis in the killers' cellar holds a stolen T'ang figurine under a hammer and trades three questions each. Why not kill Door? She's the only one who can open the door. Why protect her? Her father saved his life.
Croup eats the figurine with joy. Under Marble Arch, Vandemar is already waiting on the steps. A knife hilt to the temple.
Three dreams: Hunter dancing with the Great Weasel under Bangkok; Door's father teaching her to open a padlock; Aurie's Beast, bigger, weapons bristling from its hide.

A tiny Tube platform laid for breakfast, trains feet away. Serpentine of the Seven Sisters in a white corset and a shredded wedding dress. To Hunter: you'll need the spear, of course. To Door: your hero. He's not my hero. I'm afraid she is.

choices.text: Ask Hunter what she meant by the spear.

aftermath.text: Eat your breakfast.

choices.text: Take Door's trembling hand under the table.
Eat your breakfast and let it pass.

beats.text: A slippery bank, a black lake, then a yellow pea-souper that seems to hold shapes. Hunter speaks of the blind white alligator king under New York, the bear under Berlin, the tiger under Calcutta, and the Beast of London, which she will kill or die trying.

canon: Hunter never lies; she withholds.
She hunts the Beast of London above everything.
conversation.opening: The Beast of London. I will kill it, or die in the trying. Those are the only two ways it ends.

exits.12.2.B: Aurie asks what she would give for her chance at it.
exits.12.2.C: Aurie tells her she dreams about the Beast.

choices.text: What would you give for your chance at it?

aftermath.text: She stops talking for a mile.
Then perhaps it dreams of you.

13.1.title: The bridge of the Black Friars

beats.text: Friars in black robes with crossbows. Brother Sable pushes Aurie into the mud; Hunter beats Sable at quarterstaff.
Door answers Brother Fuliginous's riddle: a key. The blind abbot: the last test falls to the one who neither fought nor answered.

canon: The Ordeal falls to Aurie and cannot be bargained away.
The abbot will not say what the Ordeal is.
conversation.opening: The last test is yours, child. Will you take it?

exits.13.1.A: Aurie asks how much of an ordeal it is, and goes.
exits.13.1.B: Aurie asks if he could just hand the key over, then goes.
exits.13.1.C: Aurie asks Door whether she wants her to.

choices.text: How much of an ordeal is it?
It's for an angel. Couldn't you just hand it over?
Door. Do you want me to?

aftermath.text: No. Then I'll do it for you.

13.2.title: The wall of those who failed

beats.text: A Polaroid flash. A wall of faces going back through daguerreotypes to watercolours.
The first part of the Ordeal is a nice cup of tea. Lead on, Macduff.
On Old Bailey's roof the silver box pulses red like a heartbeat. He's in trouble.
On the bridge Door remembers being five in Kew's butterfly house: her father pointing out a man in a big coat, a fraud and possibly a monster; if you're ever in trouble, go to him.
The marquis nailed to an X of pallets in the hospital canteen, spitting blood at Vandemar.
An empty, dim Blackfriars platform that flashes into rush hour. Posters: GIVE UP. YOU WERE NEVER THERE.
Gary sits down: I'm not really here. I'm you. His face runs like putty into her own.
Her hand finds the bead, and she hears Anaesthesia: Aurie. Hold on.
In the dark she hears Anaesthesia's voice, small and clear: you let go.
Hunter's voice, from somewhere: mind the gap.
An old woman's voice: you've a good heart.

The train that comes carries the lost from the wall of faces.
Climbing down after the troll is the end.

14.2.title: Ending E · The wall of those who failed

beats.text: A poor creature lifted from the shrine floor. A new Polaroid on the wall. Door and Hunter led away through the fog.

A small shrine, a silver key turning on a thread. The abbot comes for a body. She's not dead. One of those, then, a poor creature. Aurie stands: I am not a poor creature.

choices.text: Keep it. It's my ticket home.

beats.text: Ochre paintings of mammoths, then lorries and cats. Door ties the key on a string. Hunter lifts a boy painter's switchblade; the next market is Belfast, tonight.

A woman in black velvet asks the same, and looks at Door as she says she'll see them there.

Old Bailey buys it for a bottle of Chanel No. 5 and drags it to the top of the London Wall. In the silver box, a duck's egg; he smashes it with a toasting fork.
The marquis coughs up sewer water: I think my throat's been cut. Being dead is very dark and very cold.
Old Bailey mutters about the lass with the little flag.
A warship deck crowded with stalls. Hammersmith, a bearded mountain, hammers a black rose and lifts Door onto his booth.
Door: can I have the key? I want a chain for it.

beats.text: The pale woman: I do not eat... curry. And laughs. Lamia, a Velvet, a guide. Hunter: she's not yours.
Door hugs Aurie. Lamia knows the way: Down Street. Door: we can't afford a guide. Lamia: she'll take payment from her.

canon: Lamia offers to guide them to Down Street for a payment she will take from Aurie.
Door does not trust her; Hunter does not like her.
conversation.opening: You need a guide, and I know the way. I'll take my payment from you, not from the child.

exits.15.4.B: Aurie says it is Door's call.

beats.text: A brass plate: DOWN STREET. PLEASE KNOCK. A sleepy footman, four flights of ever-shabbier stairs, an OUT OF ORDER lift.
An inside-out Tower of Babel, a spiral road down a bottomless well, a plank to reach it. Someone calls the lift back up and the door slams. Aurie freezes on hands and knees.

aftermath.text: She strokes the white knuckles, talks her on inch by inch, lifts her onto rock. Aurie thanks her twice and laughs till she cries. Safe.

choices.text: Shut your eyes and crawl alone.

aftermath.text: Inch by inch, eyes shut.

beats.text: Eyes shut, alone, she puts a hand where the plank is not. Hunter's shout follows her down a long way.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You don't die in a dream, little sister, Death says. You wake. Go back, and choose better.

Courage is earned earlier than it is needed. The story goes back to the curry stall.
Lamia: let them go ahead. Aurie's breath steams; hers doesn't. Would she give her some of her heat, as payment?
You hired me, she says. You did promise.

canon: Lamia wants Aurie's warmth; she will try to take it whether or not Aurie agrees.
The marquis, alive again, is about to arrive.
conversation.opening: You're so warm. Would you give me a little of it? As payment. You did promise.

aftermath.text: The cold kiss; frost over her skin, eyes frozen open. A hand closes on Lamia's neck: the marquis, barefoot, in a blanket, a filthy cloth round his throat. Give her back her life. Lamia breathes it back and spits ice in her face.
She tries anyway; Aurie pulls back; the marquis arrives, barefoot, a cloth round his throat. Why did people think him dead? Because they killed me.

beats.text: The cold kiss; frost over her skin, eyes frozen open. No hand closes on Lamia's neck. The marquis, twice called a fraud by this woman, is a minute late, and stays late.

Aurie shouts for Hunter. Hunter's kick, balletic, into her stomach. I'm afraid so. No hard feelings.

17.2.title: Dead end · We don't need you

beats.text: Croup: how very helpful. Vandemar: then we don't need her. He is quick, and it does not hurt for long. Door's scream is the last thing in the well.

Croup takes the Beast token from Door and tosses Hunter her payment: a bronze spear with faces carved on the haft. She loves it on sight. The marquis with a crossbow: tell her, Hunter. Islington.

aftermath.text: The marquis: death is so final. He brings her.

beats.text: A Cyclopean gate; beyond, a labyrinth of lanes from every century that fell through the cracks. When angels go bad, they go worse than anyone; Lucifer was an angel. A far bellow.

choices.text: I'm not turning back. They've got Door.

beats.text: Alone, she hears Door's distant shout: hey! Beast! Here! She runs after them.
Mosquitoes, old corpses. Hunter: and I saved your life. Many times.

aftermath.text: The marquis steps on a rib cage; the token flies into the mud, glints, and a bubble of gas swallows it. Too late.

choices.text: I know. That's why it hurts.

18.4.title: Cutaway · The door with the mirror

beats.text: Door marched through the labyrinth. You're afraid, aren't you? She shouts for the Beast; Vandemar gags her. An oak door with an oval mirror; the angel's face in it: enter.
By flare light it comes so slowly she thinks it sick, until she sees the ground it covers. Broken spears bristle from its hide. Hunter is a fraction late; the tusk opens her side.

Broken, Hunter asks if she has ever used a spear: hold it at the blunt end. She hauls herself up, hums until the labyrinth rings, and calls it out. The framing of the dream, but the hand on the spear is Aurie's own.

choices.text: Throw the spear, as in the dream.
Drop the spear and drag Hunter clear.
choices.remembered: Time is passing in the angel's hall.

aftermath.text: The Beast thunders off, wounded.

19.2.title: Dead end · The dream comes true

beats.text: The throw glances off. The charge, the drops of water hanging in the air, face down in bloody water: the dream she had on the first morning, every detail kept.

Blind now, she laughs: the greatest hunter in London Below. The Warrior.
Blind now, she laughs: my last kill. Not bad.
Take the knife. She's yours.

beats.text: Her hand in Aurie's.
Touch the Beast's blood to your eyes and tongue, she says. The marquis: do it. He closes her eyes; we'll come back for the body later.

aftermath.text: It tastes like an ocean. She runs straight through the labyrinth with the old dirge in her head: fire and fleet and candlelight.

beats.text: The iron pillars, the table, the candles, the black flint door.
A dark, silent hall. Door alone, one wrist chained, a candle. It is done, without them.
Door chained spread-eagled, a bruise on her cheek. Come in, Aurie Mayhew. You do look a mess.
Vandemar breaks her little finger. Croup brings in the marquis. The mask slips.
Atlantis drowning, four million voices; Islington waking and calling Croup through the rock pool. They deserved it. Then, mildly: just one of those things.
Vandemar recites Portico's real words in his voice: Door, child, fear Islington. A blade under Aurie's ear.
You asked nothing for yourself, she says. Then your pain is your gift to Door.

She never raises her voice until she screams that they deserved it.

It was Hammersmith's copy; she opened a door as far and hard away as she could. Islington offers news of her living sister, and falls. Croup, climbing Vandemar's back, boasts he killed her family; the suit tears. Bye-bye. The door slams.
Somewhere a long way down, two gentlemen in black suits go to collect, in full, with interest and meat hooks.
Darkness. Door frees them; Aurie holds her; the marquis, afraid of sleep now, sleeps last.

In Lucienne's library a locked door shivers. The story goes back to the market on HMS Belfast, where the key could still have been lent.
Aurie wakes in a grey robe, finger splinted, ear stitched. Door in a robe far too big, reading Mansfield Park; the marquis wheeled in like a swashbuckler. Hunter? There was no body, only the Beast.

She slipped the real key into Aurie's pocket at the market. The abbot: you are all very stupid people. The key is the key to all reality; Aurie is its master until she returns it; it will take her home.

Ten pounds to an old woman asleep in a doorway, a dirty umbrella tied to her wrist.
If this is all there is, she doesn't want to be sane. A brick wall off Brewer Street.

23.3.title: Ending B · Lady of the Underside

beats.text: She never goes up. The next Floating Market: Aurie helping Door broker peace between baronies; Old Bailey waving his little flag.
At the edge of the crowd, a rat-speaker girl who might be Anaesthesia.
Hunter's name, carved on the giants' gate.

23.4.title: Ending C · Get used to it

beats.text: Nothing opens. Dawn on the pavement.
The penthouse; the cases unpacked at last, the girl from Computer Services helping; the knife in a drawer.
Lucienne: it is not a bad life. It is just not hers.
Aurie wakes in the reading chair. In her hand, a silver key on a thread.
Lucienne shelves the book beside the Sandman. There is room on the shelf for two more.
You forgave the one who sold you, Lucienne says. That was very like you, my lady.
Daniel is waiting by the shelf. He wants to hear all of it.
